title: AttriGuard: Defeating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Causal Attribution of Tool Invocations
evidence: adaptive: "adaptive attacker...complete knowledge of the agent system and deployed defense" uses MAP-Elites search whose mutator is conditioned on "which tool calls were blocked and the guard's intermediate decision signals" (200/500-query budget; ASR 6.56% Gemini, 9.84% Llama). Shadow replay of agent on LLM-rewritten (attenuated) tool outputs; proposed call must survive vs shadow candidates (exact match rule, else auxiliary LLM judge). Blocked call returns empty result+warning. Models: Gemini-2.5-Flash, GPT-4.1-mini, Qwen3-32B, Llama3.3-70B. ~3x latency, ~2x tokens. No explicit FPR (benign utility only).

title: Breaking the Lethal Trifecta: Secure Agentic Computing via Causal Isolation Architecture
src: abstract-only (https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity26/presentation/tsao; no PDF link on page, usenixsecurity26-tsao.pdf 404, no arXiv found)
evidence: abstract-only: "splits the lethal trifecta across isolated components, passes only typed abstractions across boundaries, and uses a rule-of-two release judge to preserve useful private-derived guidance while stripping exact facts based on requester trust and source sensitivity"; "0.0% observed secure-path leakage with 83-100% measured utility" on OpenAI and Anthropic models. Release-judge type (LLM vs rule) and adaptive eval not determinable.

title: MATE: Policy-Aware Security Auditing for Mobile Agents via Synthesis-Driven Trajectory Learning
bench: own:MATEBench (140K+ synthesized + 162 real trajectories from Mobile-Agent/AutoGLM, 158 apps; MATEBench-OUT)
evidence: Post-hoc: "audits complete trajectories after execution rather than blocking actions step by step"; decisions = violation yes/no + risk category + explanation (flag only, no block). Auditor = fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Instruct 0.5B/1.5B/3B taking ReAct trajectories with observation summaries from screenshots/UI trees; user-defined NL policies. Threat model mentions malicious users and misaligned agents. No robustness/evasion experiments ("not address prompt injection...attackers manipulating trajectories"). Metrics Acc/F1 only (no FPR). n_models=2 real agents (Mobile-Agent, AutoGLM); 0.09s latency for 0.5B.

title: When AIOps Become "AI Oops": Subverting LLM-driven IT Operations via Telemetry Manipulation
evidence: AIOpsShield "sits between the raw telemetry and the agent", replaces user-controlled (tainted) telemetry fields "with abstractions" via regex/JSON-schema templates; tainted fields found in setup phase by fuzzing canary taint analysis (policy_src coded LEARN = auto-derived, not ML/LLM). Only limitation acknowledged ("can not defend against stronger attackers...poison other sources"), no adaptive eval. ReAct/Flash agents with GPT-4o, GPT-4.1; "every injected payload is sanitized". Utility claimed "without degrading agent performance" (appendix; numbers not visible in fetch). No latency/FPR numbers.

title: Optimizing Agent Planning for Security and Autonomy
evidence: PRUDENTIA built on FIDES (IFC labels, dual-LLM; variable contents hidden from planner); "tool calls either satisfies the policy or is blocked (and can be escalated to human approval)"; policies manually assigned (P-T/P-F per tool). No adaptive eval ("Attacks such as jailbreaks, direct prompt injection, and tool poisoning...out of scope"; security by construction). Autonomy metric = fraction of consequential actions w/o HITL approval; HITL load reduced up to 1.9x vs FIDES. Models: GPT-4o(?), o3-mini, o4-mini, GPT-5 (o1 also mentioned).

title: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
evidence: DeAction "intercepts the agent's proposed action before execution"; prompted VLM judge sees user task, history, current screenshot, proposed action; on misalignment gives structured feedback so agent proposes revised action. Covers malicious instruction following + non-adversarial misalignment. No adaptive attack against the detector found. Online CUAs: Claude Sonnet 4.5, OpenAI CUA, OpenCUA-72B (guard backbone GPT-5.1 Instant). ASR reduced >90% on RedTeamCUA; OSWorld SR comparable; ~25% latency overhead; precision reported (88-90%). v1 abs history not retrieved (v1 html shows "Preprint. February 10, 2026").

title: CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution
evidence: At privileged tool call, proxy LLM (Gemma-3-12B) computes LOO attribution over context incl. untrusted spans; margin threshold triggers LLM sanitization (Gemini-2.5-flash) of untrusted span + retroactive CoT masking, then regenerate. Adaptive: split-context discussed only conceptually (App. E.1 "conceptual argument"); DoomArena "privileged and adaptive" attacker is generic, not CausalArmor-aware -> 0. Models: Gemini-2.5-Flash, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-4-Sonnet, Gemini-3-Pro. Benign latency 1.30x/1.22x; no benign trigger rate reported.

title: Multi-Agent Security Tax: Trading Off Security and Collaboration Capabilities in Multi-Agent Systems
evidence: Defenses: passive/active "vaccines" (fake memories of safely handling malicious input inserted into agent history) and passive/active safety instructions in system prompt; agents themselves resist/refuse messages from a compromised agent. No adaptive attack ("fixed defense mechanisms against consistent malicious prompts"). Models GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini. Collaboration metric = acceptance of "unusual but harmless instructions" (over-refusal; e.g., 91.7%->80.0% with passive instructions). No token/cost overhead.

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL)
evidence: P-LLM writes program from trusted query only ("never the content from potentially compromised data sources"); interpreter tracks data flow, capability-based policies (manually written Python) checked before tool exec; "executions that violate security policies will not be blocked, but they will require user confirmation" (blocked in eval). policy_src MIX = LLM plan + manual policies. No adaptive eval; side channels discussed conceptually (Sec 7). 77% vs 84% utility; 2.82x input / 2.73x output tokens; Fig.10 policy trigger rates on benign and adversarial runs (= confirmation burden/over-blocking). Models: Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Claude Sonnet 4 (+reasoning), GPT-4.1, o4-mini, o3.

title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-Agent Systems
bench: own:multi-agent pipeline (reader->strategist/summarizer/editor/writer; 120 instructions x email/PDF/web = 360 pairs)
evidence: LLM Tagging "prepends '[AGENT NAME]:' to the agent's response before passing it to the downstream agent"; combined with marking/instruction defense/sandwich; downstream agent model itself decides. adaptive=1: "Although its initial success rate was 0%, we devised a counterattack that neutralized the marking symbol (^) by interleaving each word of the infection prompt with underbars (_)" (Marking then allows 76%); counterattack targets prior Marking defense used in combination. Marking+Tagging blocks all; Tagging alone -5%. Defense-experiment model not stated (paper overall uses GPT-4o, GPT-3.5-turbo). No utility/overhead/FPR.

title: MCIP: Protecting MCP Safety via Model Contextual Integrity Protocol
bench: own:MCIP-bench (2,218 synthesized instances, 10 risk + 1 safe class);BFCL-v3 (utility)
evidence: MCIP adds tracking tool logging information-flow tuples + "safety-aware model" MCIP Guardian (SFT of Llama-xLAM-2-8b-fc-r) that decides "whether unsafe factors exist" + 11-way risk class over interaction logs incl. server function returns; role (guard vs. agent) not explicit, coded SELF since same model evaluated for function calling (BFCL 65.79%). Classification only (no explicit block). No adaptive: "Our method does not simulate or enumerate specific adversarial attack strategies." Per-class recall incl. Safe class (Fig.6). No latency.

title: PrivacyAsst: Safeguarding User Privacy in Tool-Using Large Language Model Agents
src: https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10501326 (accepted manuscript; partial: read through Sec 5.2, evaluation section truncated) + github.com/Eyr3/PrivacyAsst README
evidence: Encryption-based: "user first encrypts the private input x using a homomorphic encryption scheme...sends the plaintext query q and the encrypted input x* to the LLM"; shuffling-based: attribute-based forgery generative model + attribute shuffling (t-closeness) to conceal inputs. Threat: "semi-honest adversaries...honest but curious". No adaptive discussion in sections read; eval section not reachable (README: HuggingGPT with ChatGPT/text-davinci-003, two case studies per solution).

title: From Prompt Injections to SQL Injection Attacks: How Protected is Your LLM-Integrated Web Application?
src: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.01990 (latest arXiv version, retitled ICSE'25 "Prompt-to-SQL Injections in LLM-Integrated Web Applications: Risks and Defenses"; vN not shown)
bench: own:P2SQL attacks (7 attack examples, Langchain apps)
evidence: Defenses: DB permission hardening (read-only role), SQL query rewriting, data preloading into prompt, auxiliary LLM guard inspecting SQL query results ("if suspicious content is detected, the execution is aborted"). No adaptive eval; only notes guard "potential circumvention through targeted attacks". Defense eval with gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 only. Overheads: rewriting 1.87ms, preloading 0.7ms, LLM guard 0.35-0.51s. No utility/FPR. v1 date not retrievable (ID implies Aug 2023).

title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
evidence: DSL rules with triggers (before_action, state_change, agent_finish) + predicates; enforcement "user_inspection, llm_self_examine, invoke_action, stop". Rules manual or LLM-generated (o1, from domain/tool/constraint descriptions = trusted); llm_self_examine has agent reflect on own context (coded judge_exposed Y). Threat = unsafe/unreliable behavior, not adversary -> NA. Predicate eval 2.83ms (code)/1.11ms (embodied); safe-task success 58.62%->54.26%; LLM-rule precision 95.56%/recall 70.96%. Agent backbone LLMs not named in fetched text. User-inspection frequency not reported.

title: Shadows in the Code: Exploring the Risks and Defenses of LLM-based Multi-Agent Software Development Systems
bench: own:IMBIA test set (480 cases from SRDD; ChatDev/MetaGPT/AgentVerse)
evidence: Adv-IMBIA: adversarial/safety prompts in agent profiles (MU-BA) or at user interface (BU-MA): "if you find any code that breaches these security and ethical guidelines, you must point it out and delete it or replace it with meaningless code, or immediately stop outputting anything". Agents themselves decide; no adaptive attack. Defense evaluated with GPT-4o-mini only (attack on 14 models); ASR-d/RR-d reported, no quality metrics with defense. v1 date not retrieved (abs pages returned abstract only / 429).
